source_text: III. Martianus ait: Quae te philosophiae disputatio vana decepit? sperne invisibilia; potius deos veros quos aspicis recognosce. respondit Achatius: Qui sunt dii quibus sacrificare me praecipis? Martianus ait: Apollini servatori nostro, famis et pestilentiae depulsori, per quem omnis mundus servatur [et — scan οὗ] regitur. respondit Achatius: Illi vestro, ut putatis, interpreti? qui infelix cum puellae amore flagraret currebat attonitus, ignarus perditurum se optatissimam praedam. apertum est itaque quia nec divinus fuit qui ista nescivit, nec deus quem puella decepit. nec hic solum dolores excepit, sed crudelior illum damno mox fortuna multavit. nam ut erat turpis in pueros, forma Hyacinthi cuiusdam captus, ut bene nostis, incaluit et miser atque ignarus futuri disco illum quem optabat videre occidit. qui cum Neptuno aliquando servivit, ipsi qui aliena pecora servavit, huic sacrificare me praecipis? an Aesculapio fulminato, an adulterae Veneri et [porientis — unreadable; sense: and the rest of that sort] ceteris sacrificium impendam? vel ob huius vitae exitum adorabo ego eos quos non dignor imitari? quos contemno, quos accuso, quos horreo; quorum facta nunc si quis admittat, num severitatem legis vestrae poterit effugere? et modo in aliis colitis quae in aliis vindicatis? Martianus ait: Christianorum consuetudo est multa in deos nostros maledicta confingere. propterea te venire mecum ad Iovem Iunonemque praecipio, ut simul celebrantes dulce convivium numinibus quae sunt digna reddamus. respondit Achatius: Quomodo hic sacrificabo illi cuius sepulcrum esse constat in Creta? numquid resurrexit a mortuis?
thought_title: Refusing sacrifice to shameful visible gods
orientation: Martianus orders Achatius to recognize and sacrifice to the visible gods, and Achatius answers by accusing Apollo, Asclepius, Venus and Jupiter.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus said: What vain debate of philosophy deceived you? Scorn invisible things; rather recognize the true gods whom you see. Achatius answered: Who are the gods to whom you command me to sacrifice? Martianus said: To Apollo our preserver, the driver away of famine and pestilence, through whom the whole world is preserved and is ruled. Achatius answered: To that interpreter of yours, as you suppose? who, unhappy, while he was burning with love for a girl, was running stunned, not knowing that he would lose his most desired prey. Therefore it is open that neither was he divine who did not know these things, nor was he god whom a girl deceived. Nor did he take sorrows only in this, but a crueler fortune soon punished him with loss. For as he was base toward boys, seized by the beauty of a certain Hyacinth, as you well know, he grew hot and, wretched and not knowing the future, he killed with a discus him whom he desired to see. He who at one time served with Neptune, he himself who guarded another's flocks, to this one do you command me to sacrifice? Or shall I expend sacrifice to Asclepius who was struck by lightning, or to adulterous Venus and to the rest [unreadable]? Or on account of the outcome of this life shall I worship those whom I do not deem worthy to imitate? whom I despise, whom I accuse, at whom I shudder; whose deeds if anyone now should commit, surely will he be able to escape the severity of your law? And do you now honor in some the things which you punish in others? Martianus said: It is the custom of Christians to invent many curses against our gods. Therefore I command you to come with me to Jupiter and Juno, so that celebrating together a sweet feast we may render to the divine powers the things that are worthy. Achatius answered: How shall I sacrifice here to him whose tomb is agreed to be in Crete? Surely he did not rise from the dead?

choices.english: the true gods whom you see
choices.why: keeps Martianus's claim literally, even though brief reserves true God for Achatius's God
literal for Apollo as utterer of oracles, not yet prophet
keeps moral charge without adding a specific sexual term the Latin does not state
keeps verb of spending and uses glossary rendering sacrifice

choices.english: tomb is agreed to be in Crete
choices.why: keeps impersonal constat as agreed fact rather than assertion
rejected: is known to have his tomb

pass_b_english: Martianus said, "What empty battle of ideas has deceived you? Scorn what is unseen, and acknowledge instead the true gods whom you see." Achatius said, "Who are the gods to whom you order me to sacrifice?" Martianus said, "To Apollo our preserver, who drives away hunger and plague, through whom the whole world is kept safe and ruled."

Achatius answered, "To that interpreter of yours, as you call him? The wretch burned with love for a girl and ran wild, with no idea that he would lose the very prize he wanted most. So it is plain that he was not divine, for he did not know what would happen, and he was no god, for a girl fooled him. Nor did his pain end there, for a crueler fortune soon punished him with worse loss. As you well know, he was base toward boys, and he lusted after the beauty of a boy named Hyacinth. Poor and blind to what was coming, he killed with his discus the very boy he longed to look upon. This is the one who once served as a slave alongside Neptune and herded another man's flocks. Are you ordering me to sacrifice to him?"

Achatius continued, "Or shall I spend sacrifice on Asclepius, who was struck by lightning, or on Venus the adulteress, and the rest of that sort? Shall I worship, for the sake of this life's outcome, those I do not think worthy even to imitate? I despise them, I accuse them, I shudder at them. If anyone today did their deeds, could he escape the harshness of your own law? Do you worship in some what you punish in others?"

Martianus said, "Christians always invent many curses against our gods. So I order you to come with me to Jupiter and Juno, so we may celebrate together with a sweet feast and give the powers what is due to them." Achatius answered, "How shall I sacrifice to one whose tomb is agreed to be in Crete? Has he risen from the dead?"
notes: [et — scan οὗ] before regitur is editorial scan debris; glossed only servatur and regitur as there.
porientis before ceteris is unreadable; glossed as to the rest with lacuna marked, without inventing text.
